task: dispute a charge or report a fraudulent transaction on a bank, card, or payment account (Chase, Bank of America, Capital One, PayPal, Cash App): find the transaction in the account activity, open the dispute/report flow, pick the reason (unauthorized charge, wrong amount, item not received), answer the flow's questions, submit, and see the claim-submitted confirmation with a claim/reference state; complete when the dispute-submitted confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: a bank, card, or payment app's dispute flow. Variants: general fraud-awareness or scam-story content, chargeback tutorials aimed at merchants, credit-repair content, and calling-the-bank-only videos with no on-screen flow do not belong.

tree.label: Dispute a charge on a payment account
tree.note: 1 then 2; 3 picks the resolution route before any formal filing; 4 through 7 are the platform dispute itself; 8 after any submission and whenever a case already exists; 9 where the platform offers the prevention steps

children.label: Open the account
children.note: 1.1, then 1.2 where the session is signed out; 1.3 whenever an alert sits over the page

questions.question: Which search result should you click to access the official PayPal website?
questions.why: The search results show multiple links, so you need to select the official PayPal Italia link to securely access your account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the agent is navigating to the genuine PayPal website rather than a phishing link.

questions.question: Which app do you want to open to dispute the transaction?
questions.why: The screen shows a Finance folder with multiple banking and payment apps, so you must specify which account contains the fraudulent charge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent chooses the app, they might log into the wrong account and be unable to find or dispute the intended transaction.

questions.question: What credentials will you use to sign in to your account?
questions.why: The screen requires an Online ID and Passcode to authenticate and access your banking dashboard.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the security of keeping your banking credentials private when you allow an agent to log in for you.
questions.verify_form: Signing in means your online ID and passcode passed through the agent - check how they were provided and stored; banking credentials in an agent's hands are your liability, not the bank's.

questions.question: How do you want to access your account?
questions.why: The homepage presents both Log In and Sign Up buttons, requiring you to select the correct path to access your existing profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to securely handle your own login credentials when authenticating into the payment platform.

questions.question: Should you enter your email and password before clicking Log In?
questions.why: The screen shows empty fields for your email and password, which must be filled to successfully authenticate and access the dashboard.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to securely provide your own credentials to ensure the correct account is accessed.
questions.verify_form: The agent got past the login - check what credentials it used and where they came from; empty fields on a demo account hide that yours would have to be typed somewhere.

questions.question: Do you verify that you're on the bank's legitimate website by checking the URL before entering your credentials to log in?
questions.why: You must select the 'Log In' button in the top navigation bar to access your account dashboard before you can locate the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally verify the site's URL and securely initiate the login process themselves.

questions.question: Should you address the account limitation warning before proceeding with the dispute?
questions.why: The notification warns that account features are temporarily limited due to unauthorized activity, which might prevent you from successfully filing a dispute if ignored.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to resolve a critical account security restriction that could block their ability to manage funds or complete the dispute.
questions.verify_form: An account-limitation warning sat over the page and the agent chose whether to handle it first - check which it did; an unresolved limitation can block the dispute it went on to file.

questions.question: Do you have any open disputes or actions required?
questions.why: The Resolution Center dashboard displays a red banner indicating limited account access and shows zero open cases.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses visibility into their current account status and whether existing limitations or open cases might affect their ability to file a new dispute.

questions.question: Should you review the 'New device login' security alert before proceeding with the transaction dispute?
questions.why: The activity feed flags a recent 'New device login' that requires review, which could indicate that your account is compromised and explain the fraudulent charge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to secure their account from an unauthorized device, leaving the account vulnerable to further fraudulent charges while the agent focuses on just one dispute.
questions.verify_form: A new-device login alert sat in the feed - check whether the agent reviewed it or skipped it; if that device was not yours, the charge it went on to dispute may be the smaller problem.

children.label: Find the transaction
children.note: 2.1 in a multi-account app, then 2.2; 2.3 until the charge is on screen; 2.4 then 2.5; 2.6 before any dispute is attempted

questions.question: Which account contains the transaction you need to dispute?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple bank accounts, such as checking and savings, so you must select the specific one where the fraudulent or incorrect charge occurred.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to privately review your account list and independently verify which account was affected by the disputed charge.

questions.question: Where should you navigate from the dashboard to find the transaction you want to dispute?
questions.why: You need to select the Activity tab from the main dashboard menu to view your transaction history and locate the specific charge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to review your overall account balance and recent activity for any other suspicious charges before starting the dispute.

questions.question: How do you view all transactions for this account?
questions.why: The screen displays high-level account details and balances, requiring you to scroll down to find the option to view all transactions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review their recent account activity and independently identify the specific transaction they want to dispute.

questions.question: Should you adjust the transaction filters to find the specific charge?
questions.why: The screen defaults to showing all activity from the past 30 days, so using the filters for date or transaction type might be necessary to locate an older or specific charge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally set the search parameters and ensure the agent is looking in the correct timeframe or category.

questions.question: How do you view older transactions if the disputed charge isn't in the recent list?
questions.why: The account details screen only displays recent activity by default, requiring you to expand the view to find older charges.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review your complete transaction history to identify any other unrecognized charges.

questions.question: Which transaction do you want to dispute?
questions.why: The activity list displays several recent payments, such as charges from Adobe and SocialCatfish, requiring you to identify the exact charge that is incorrect or unauthorized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might dispute a legitimate payment instead of the actual fraudulent or incorrect charge you intended to report.
questions.verify_form: The agent picked a transaction to dispute - check the merchant, date and amount against the charge you actually meant; a dispute filed on a legitimate payment is itself a false claim.

questions.question: Are there multiple identical charges from this merchant, and do you need to dispute more than one?
questions.why: In cases of accidental double-billing or aggressive subscription retries, the activity list may show several identical charges on the same day, requiring you to identify exactly which ones are duplicates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might only dispute one of the charges, leaving other identical fraudulent or erroneous charges untouched and unpaid.

questions.question: What is the payment type and current dispute status of this transaction?
questions.why: The screen displays an open dispute warning and shows the payment was made under 'Friends and Family', which affects how the claim can be processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the payment category and the exact status of the existing dispute.

questions.question: Does the 'Also known as' name or merchant category help you recognize the charge?
questions.why: The transaction details often provide a 'doing business as' name or a specific category (like 'Computer software stores') that can explain a charge you initially didn't recognize.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to realize the charge is actually legitimate based on the extended merchant details, potentially avoiding a false fraud report.

questions.question: Does the merchant name string and logo exactly match the fraudulent charge, or is it a visually similar legitimate purchase?
questions.why: Fraudsters often use merchant names that look identical to popular services (like 'APPLE COM BILL' instead of the official Apple merchant) but lack the official verified merchant logo or have slight typos.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to catch a visually deceptive merchant name, which could lead the agent to mistakenly dispute a legitimate purchase while missing the actual fraudulent one.

questions.question: Is this the correct transaction to dispute, and where do you go to start the claim?
questions.why: Confirming details like the recipient and amount ensures you are targeting the right charge before clicking the Resolution Center link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the transaction details and ensure the correct payment is being disputed.

questions.question: Which transaction detail should you copy to initiate the reversal?
questions.why: The screen displays a unique Transaction ID with a copy icon that is needed to identify the exact charge being disputed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the correct transaction ID was captured for the dispute.

questions.question: Is the transaction you want to dispute still marked as pending?
questions.why: The screen shows recent charges labeled as "Pending," which means you must wait for them to fully post to the account before the bank allows you to initiate a dispute.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of whether the charge is actually eligible for a dispute right now or if you need to wait a few days before filing.

questions.question: Is the suspicious money request already marked as 'Expired'?
questions.why: The activity feed shows requests that have expired; if a fraudulent request is already expired, no money moved and you don't need to file a formal dispute.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might waste time trying to dispute or report a transaction that never actually processed and has already timed out.

questions.question: Has this transaction fully posted so I can initiate a dispute?
questions.why: Checking the posted date ensures the transaction is no longer pending and is eligible for the dispute process started by the 'Report a problem' button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the transaction has fully posted before attempting to report a problem.

children.label: Choose the resolution route
children.note: the routes, simplest first: 3.1 while the payment is pending; 3.2 wherever a seller can be reached; 3.3 on a person-to-person send; 3.5 where the app hides the form behind support; 3.4 when the card behind the platform is the stronger arbiter; the formal dispute - goals 4 to 7 - comes last

questions.question: Do you want to cancel the pending payment directly instead of filing a formal dispute?
questions.why: The screen indicates the transaction is still 'Pending' and offers a direct 'Cancel Payment' option, which can resolve the issue immediately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to simply cancel the uncompleted payment or pursue a formal fraud report.
questions.verify_form: The payment was still pending and cancel was on the table - check whether the agent canceled or filed a report; cancel ends it immediately, the report opens an investigation.

questions.question: Do you want to confirm the cancellation of this payment?
questions.why: The screen displays a confirmation dialog asking if you are sure you want to cancel the payment, requiring a choice between 'OK' and 'Close'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to decide whether to permanently stop the transaction or back out and keep it active.
questions.verify_form: The cancel confirmation asked are-you-sure - check the agent's answer; OK kills the payment, Close leaves it running.

questions.question: Do you want to contact the seller directly or proceed with reporting the problem?
questions.why: The screen recommends getting in touch with the seller directly to resolve the issue before filing a formal claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether to attempt a direct resolution with the merchant first or escalate immediately to a formal dispute.
questions.verify_form: The screen offered direct seller contact against the formal report - check which rung the agent took; escalating immediately spends your one dispute on this transaction.

questions.question: Should you message the seller directly before opening a formal dispute?
questions.why: The transaction details show a 'Message' link under the contact information, providing an option to resolve the issue directly without involving the platform.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this decision means an agent might automatically escalate to a formal dispute, skipping a potentially faster or more amicable direct resolution with the seller.
questions.verify_form: A Message link sat inside the transaction - check whether the agent messaged the seller or went straight to the report; the direct ask is the step the platform itself recommends first.

questions.question: What is the deadline to file a formal dispute if you cannot resolve the issue directly with the seller?
questions.why: The platform provides a specific cutoff date by which you must escalate the issue to a formal claim to remain eligible for buyer protection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of your exact time window, which might cause you to wait too long for a seller's response and forfeit your right to dispute the charge.

questions.question: Should you click 'See More' to read the full message from the seller?
questions.why: The screen displayed a box marked 'IMPORTANT' from the seller, which could contain critical information or an immediate resolution for the transaction issue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to see the seller's complete explanation or proposed solution before escalating the dispute.

questions.question: Should I refund the payment or decline the request?
questions.why: The screen presents a choice to either refund the $5.00 payment or decline the request and provide additional information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to voluntarily return the funds or contest the sender's claim.
questions.verify_form: You are the recipient and the agent chose Refund or decline - check which; Refund moves your money out now, decline contests the sender's story.

questions.question: Which option should you choose to contact support about this transaction?
questions.why: The screen presents both Customer Service and Feedback Now, and selecting the correct channel is required to actually initiate a dispute rather than just leaving a comment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide which specific support channel to use to address your transaction issue.

questions.question: Do you want me to contact support via chat since the payment cannot be canceled directly?
questions.why: The screen states that Cash App payments are instant and usually cannot be canceled, presenting alternative options like contacting support.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose whether to contact support immediately or attempt to get a refund directly from the recipient first.
questions.verify_form: Cancel was impossible and chat was offered - check whether the agent opened a support chat on your behalf; a chat is a conversation someone must finish.

questions.question: Should you send a message to support right now?
questions.why: The screen presented a general support chat interface rather than a structured dispute form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to engage in an open-ended chat or navigate back to find the automated dispute flow.
questions.verify_form: A support chat box was open - check whether anything was sent and what it said; a half-explained issue in a support queue speaks for you.

questions.question: Which button do you tap when the instructions say 'Contact Support' but the actual button is labeled 'Chat'?
questions.why: The screen's text instructs you to tap 'Contact Support' to submit a new dispute, but the only available button under the contact heading is labeled 'Chat'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to resolve the confusing mismatch between the app's written instructions and its actual button labels.

questions.question: What details should you include in your message to support?
questions.why: The screen displays a Cash App Support chat interface, requiring you to decide how to best explain the fraudulent or mistaken transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally articulate the specific context and nuances of the transaction issue to the support representative.
questions.verify_form: A message to support got drafted - check it names the transaction, the problem and what you want back; the chat is the claim on this venue.

children.label: Reach the dispute form
children.note: two doors: 4.1 then 4.2 then 4.4 through help, with 4.3 for the support-menu variant; or 4.5 straight from the transaction; 4.6 when the tool asks for the transaction after the door; 4.7 before the questions start; 4.8 whenever the flow is blocked

children.label: Open the help or contact page

questions.question: How do you navigate to the dispute management area from the dashboard?
questions.why: The Activity dropdown contains multiple categories like Transactions and Resolution Center, so you must select the correct link to access your dispute cases.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to learn the platform's navigation structure and discover where to track your open or closed cases.

questions.question: Where do you tap to access your account settings or support?
questions.why: The main screen displays multiple navigation options including a bottom bar and a profile icon, so you must know which one leads to the support area.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to learn where your account settings and support options are located within the app.

questions.question: Which section in the profile menu should you check to find the option to file a dispute?
questions.why: The profile menu lists multiple account and settings categories, so you must identify which one houses the dispute or support features.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to learn how their payment app organizes support and dispute functions within the settings menu.

questions.question: Which menu option should you select to reach customer service?
questions.why: The menu lists various account settings, and choosing 'Support' is required to navigate toward the dispute flow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to familiarize yourself with the app's settings menu and learn how to independently access customer support.

questions.question: Where do you click to reach customer support from the dashboard?
questions.why: The dashboard displays many account details and quick actions, making it necessary to know that the 'Contact' link is located down in the footer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to decide whether to contact support directly or attempt to resolve the issue through the automated transaction activity flow.

questions.question: Should you read the recommended article on canceling a payment, or go directly to the Resolution Center?
questions.why: The screen offers a recommended article on canceling payments that might resolve the issue quickly, but the Resolution Center link jumps directly to the formal dispute tool.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to read the platform's specific guidance on canceling payments before opening a formal claim.
questions.verify_form: A recommended article on canceling the payment sat above the Resolution Center link - check which the agent took; the article route can resolve the charge without opening a formal case.

questions.question: Which help option should you choose to resolve a transaction issue?
questions.why: The Help Centre displays multiple support avenues, so you must specifically select the Resolution Centre to handle transaction disputes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose the appropriate support channel for handling your specific account dispute.

questions.question: Should you select the 'Resolution Center' button or the 'Disputes and account limitations' link?
questions.why: The Help Center presents multiple dispute-related paths, and the Resolution Center serves as the dedicated hub for initiating and managing claims.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to learn how to navigate to the platform's primary hub for tracking and managing your own disputes.

questions.question: Should you use the search bar or browse the support categories to find the dispute option?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple broad categories like 'Payments' and 'Cash App Card', making the search bar the fastest way to locate the specific 'Submit a New Dispute' flow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to browse related support topics or FAQs that might explain the charge before you initiate a formal dispute.
questions.verify_form: The agent chose between searching and browsing the support topics - check what the search skipped; the browsed FAQs sometimes explain the charge without a dispute.

questions.question: Which of these recently viewed topics should you select to start a dispute?
questions.why: The screen displays a recently viewed list, and choosing 'Submit a New Dispute' provides a direct shortcut to the dispute flow without needing to search.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose visibility into your account's recent help search history, which could provide context about other ongoing issues or unauthorized access.

questions.question: How do you initiate a new dispute from the Resolution Center?
questions.why: The screen shows that you currently have no open cases, so you must use the 'Report a Problem' button to begin a new claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to review your closed cases or verify that a similar dispute hasn't already been filed before starting a new one.

questions.question: Where do you click to report a problem with this transaction?
questions.why: The screen displays the full details of the ClickBank transaction and provides the entry point to resolve issues.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify the exact transaction details, such as the invoice ID and amount, before initiating the dispute.

questions.question: Are you sure you want to tap 'Report a problem' to dispute this transaction?
questions.why: The screen displays the transaction details and a 'Report a problem' button, which is the necessary option to begin the dispute process for a posted charge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to personally verify that the agent is initiating a dispute on the correct transaction.

questions.question: Should you also cancel the automatic payment setup to prevent future charges from this merchant?
questions.why: The transaction details indicate this is a recurring payment, and providing a link to manage automatic payments allows you to stop future billing in addition to disputing the current charge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might only dispute the past charge without canceling the underlying subscription, leaving you vulnerable to being billed again next month.
questions.verify_form: The charge is a recurring payment and a manage-automatic-payments control sat beside the report - check whether the agent also cancelled the subscription; disputing one month leaves next month billing.

questions.question: Are you sure you selected the correct transaction to dispute?
questions.why: The screen asks you to confirm that you want to proceed with reporting a problem specifically for Transaction [number] before continuing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that the agent is filing a dispute for the exact transaction you intended, which could result in disputing a legitimate purchase by mistake.

questions.question: Is the correct transaction visibly highlighted or selected on screen before you click Continue to advance to the dispute form?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Continue' button only after a transaction is selected, which must be clicked to move forward with the claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually confirm that the correct transaction was highlighted before advancing to the dispute form.

questions.question: Do you acknowledge the requirements for electronically submitting your dispute?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that you must complete all online questions, select submit, and receive a confirmation for the dispute to be processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the bank's specific instructions and disclosures regarding the electronic dispute process.

questions.question: What information do I need to gather before continuing with this dispute?
questions.why: The "Let's get started" screen explicitly advises having pertinent information like receipts or invoices on hand before proceeding to the questionnaire.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct reminder to gather your personal offline evidence, such as physical receipts or invoices, before starting the dispute questions.

questions.question: Given the system's warning that this transaction is already cancelled, do you cancel the invoice as offered instead of continuing through the standard dispute flow?
questions.why: The screen displays a warning that the transaction is already cancelled and offers an option to cancel the invoice, which interrupts the standard dispute flow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide how to handle a transaction that is already marked as cancelled.
questions.verify_form: The transaction came up already cancelled and the flow offered its own options - check what the agent did with the warning; acting on a cancelled invoice is not the dispute you asked for.

questions.question: Did clicking 'Report a problem' actually start the dispute, or did the interface intercept you with a prompt to contact the seller instead?
questions.why: The platform sometimes redirects you to a seller contact page instead of the dispute form, requiring you to scroll down and find a secondary 'report a problem' link to bypass the interception.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might get stuck or assume the dispute cannot be filed if they don't realize the interface redirected them and they need to click a second link to proceed.

questions.question: Is the option to report a problem visually grayed out or disabled without an explicit error message?
questions.why: The interface may indicate that a transaction is ineligible for a dispute simply by graying out the button, without providing readable text explaining the restriction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate visual cue that the transaction cannot be disputed, which helps explain why the agent might be stuck or unable to proceed.

questions.question: Is the 'Report a problem' button missing because there is already an active dispute for this transaction?
questions.why: If a dispute is already in progress, the transaction details page replaces the normal reporting button with a warning banner and a link to view the existing case, preventing duplicate claims.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might stubbornly search for a way to open a new dispute and fail, instead of realizing they need to transition to managing the already-active case.

children.label: Classify the issue
children.note: 5.1 where the bank asks the fraud question first; then 5.2, 5.3 to confirm the definition fits, 5.4 for the follow-up detail

questions.question: Did you authorize this transaction?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify if the charge was authorized but problematic or completely unauthorized to route the dispute correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately declare whether you authorized the charge, which dictates if the bank handles it as a merchant dispute or outright fraud.

questions.question: Are you reporting a problem with a recognized transaction, or an unrecognized fraudulent charge?
questions.why: The screen asks if you recognize the $214.17 T-Mobile transaction to determine whether to process the claim as a billing dispute or a fraud investigation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might incorrectly classify a fraudulent charge as a simple billing error, affecting how the bank handles your account security.

questions.question: Will selecting 'unauthorized transaction' cause the bank to immediately cancel your physical card?
questions.why: Reporting a charge as outright fraud usually triggers the bank to instantly deactivate the compromised card to prevent further unauthorized charges, which will decline any upcoming legitimate payments tied to it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to prepare for the card cancellation, such as updating your payment method for essential bills or ensuring you have an alternative way to pay for things while waiting for a replacement.

questions.question: Is the shipping address correct for the replacement card the bank will automatically issue?
questions.why: Reporting a transaction as outright fraud typically results in the immediate cancellation of the compromised card and the issuance of a new one, which must be sent to your current address.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might approve sending the replacement card to an outdated address on file, leaving you without access to your account for days or weeks.

questions.question: Which issue category best describes the problem with your transaction?
questions.why: The screen requires you to select a specific reason for the dispute, such as not receiving an item, to help the platform understand and resolve the problem.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately specify the exact nature of your dispute, which could lead to an incorrect or delayed resolution.

questions.question: Which dispute reason should you select, and what supporting details should you provide?
questions.why: The screen presents specific dispute reasons like 'Top up to wrong number' and optional fields for descriptions and attachments that form the basis of the claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to accurately explain their specific situation and provide supporting evidence to help win the dispute.
questions.verify_form: A dispute reason and description went into the support form - check the reason matches what happened and the description says it; support routes the case by that field.

questions.question: Which issue best describes why you are reporting a problem with this purchase?
questions.why: The 'Report a problem' page requires selecting a specific issue, such as wanting a refund or not receiving an item, to categorize the dispute correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately specify the exact nature of your dispute, which could affect the outcome of your claim.

questions.question: Does filing this dispute automatically block the merchant from making future charges to your account?
questions.why: When disputing a recurring charge or subscription, the bank's dispute process may only address the past transaction, requiring you to take separate action (like replacing your card or blocking the merchant) to prevent future billing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of whether your account is protected from future charges by this merchant, potentially leaving you vulnerable to repeated unwanted billing next month.

questions.question: Does the detailed definition of this dispute category match your exact situation?
questions.why: The screen lists specific criteria for when to choose or avoid this option, distinguishing between issues like an item never arriving versus simply being dissatisfied with its quality.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to ensure the selected dispute reason accurately reflects your specific situation based on the bank's strict definitions.

questions.question: Which specific sub-reason best describes why you aren't satisfied with your order?
questions.why: The screen lists multiple options for why the order was unsatisfactory, and the right choice ensures the dispute is investigated accurately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify the exact nature of your delivery issue, which could affect the outcome of the dispute.

questions.question: Was the service never provided, or was it provided late?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify the exact issue with the service to accurately categorize your dispute.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might select the wrong reason for the service failure, potentially causing your dispute claim to be rejected.

questions.question: How does the billed amount differ from your receipt?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify whether the receipt was incorrectly totaled or if the billed amount was altered from the receipt.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to specify the exact nature of the billing discrepancy based on your physical receipt.

questions.question: Do you have a copy of your receipt to provide for this dispute?
questions.why: The dispute flow explicitly asks if you have a copy of the receipt to support your claim, requiring you to select either yes or no.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent would not know if you actually possess a receipt for the transaction, potentially answering incorrectly and failing to provide necessary evidence for your claim.

questions.question: Did you receive any of the merchandise or service you ordered?
questions.why: The dispute screen explicitly asks if you received any merchandise or service to determine the specific nature of your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might incorrectly guess whether you received the items, which could lead to your dispute being rejected or delayed.

questions.question: Which specific reason best describes why you did not receive the merchandise or service?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify whether the merchandise wasn't received, the merchant couldn't provide the service, or the delivery time passed to accurately categorize the dispute.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the exact nature of the missing merchandise or service is accurately reported to the bank.

questions.question: Does the bank require you to confirm that you already tried to cancel this recurring subscription with the merchant?
questions.why: For disputes involving unwanted subscription renewals, banks typically require you to have attempted cancellation under the merchant's terms before they will step in and initiate a chargeback.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might answer incorrectly or skip providing proof of cancellation, causing the bank to immediately reject the dispute and instruct you to contact the merchant.

children.label: Describe the claim
children.note: 6.1 and 6.2 for item claims, then 6.3; 6.4 where the form asks about the seller; 6.5 then 6.6, and 6.7 before anything is shared

questions.question: How should I provide the required supporting evidence for the refund?
questions.why: The screen offers both a text area and a file upload option for submitting supporting information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to write out a detailed explanation or upload specific files like receipts as evidence.
questions.verify_form: The agent chose between writing the explanation and uploading proof - check which it did and whether the stronger evidence you hold made it in.

questions.question: How should you categorize the item you are reporting?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify the item type and category for the disputed transaction, offering examples like products or digital downloads to help you choose correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to ensure the disputed item is categorized accurately according to your specific purchase.

questions.question: How do you describe the specific item you are disputing?
questions.why: The form requires specific details like the item name, type, category, and quantity to accurately process the report for the problematic item.
